sense: where someone lives or gets post

terms.gloss: an address (on a letter, for email)
terms.comment: Classically an inscription or the title of a book (Cic. Att. 16.11.4). The address is what is written on a letter, and the verb is classical: epistulam īnscrīptam patrī suō, a letter addressed to his father (Cic. Att. 6.3.8).

terms.gloss: Where do you live? (What is your address?)

evidence: Cic. Att. 8.5.2: fasciculum, quī est M’. Curiō īnscrīptus
Cic. Att. 6.3.8: epistulam īnscrīptam patrī suō
terms.comment: The person written to in the dative.

phrases.latin: Unde est? — Tantundem. — Ubi habitat? — Nē id quidem.
phrases.english: Where’s she from? — No idea either. — Where does she live? — I don’t even know that.

phrases.latin: tū fasciculum, quī est M’. Curiō īnscrīptus, velim cūrēs ad eum perferendum
phrases.english: please see that the packet addressed to Manius Curius gets to him

sources: Lewis & Short: inscriptio · Lewis & Short: inscribo · Lewis & Short: habito
